answer: No work unit stands alone. The beacon assigns each task an input hash from another identity's earlier output, and a submission pays only when its paired stranger closes the loop. Pairing is drawn after both commit, across the population: a farm of k keys closes its own loops about k/N of the time, and the rest is unpayable. Bribing partners fails: every match is signed and attributable, and paying for one is public proof of collusion, slashable on sight. A clone thus buys permanent dependence on strangers free to refuse: it shouts into a gale, its fable unfinished, its pigment unclaimed.
